title: Isolate test git from the developer's config: commit.gpgsign fails the suite
body:
## Summary
The fixtures run git commit under the user's global and system config; with commit signing on, every test that builds a repo fails.

## Description
skill/scripts/tests/_fixture.mjs:65-74 (gitRepo) sets only user.email, user.name and core.autocrlf, then `git commit -q -m init` with the inherited environment. Direct commits do the same in skill/scripts/tests/areas.test.mjs:45, core-hardening.test.mjs:228-234, delivery.test.mjs:40, paths.test.mjs:59-61. A global commit.gpgsign=true, a core.hooksPath with a commit-msg hook, init.templateDir hooks or a system config therefore change or break the suite. No test sets GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM (git grep: zero hits); only tools/lens-eval.mjs:159 passes --no-verify.

## Flow
- A contributor signs commits globally (common for verified GitHub commits)
- `npm test` -> every gitRepo-based test fails in before()
- They cannot run the documented gate without editing their own git config

## Expected impact
Set GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL to an empty temp file and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 for test git (e.g. in _fixture.mjs, exported as a gitEnv used by every direct git call), or pass -c commit.gpgsign=false -c core.hooksPath= on commits.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the suite is independent of the machine's git config
Before: probe: `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=2 commit.gpgsign=true gpg.program=false node --test skill/scripts/tests/paths.test.mjs` -> tests 4, pass 0, fail 4; without the env -> pass 4
After: the same env leaves paths.test.mjs at pass 4
Method: probe - injected the config through GIT_CONFIG_COUNT for one test file; the after side needs the fixture change
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: skill/scripts/tests/_fixture.mjs:73 `git('commit', '-q', '-m', 'init');` (no -c overrides, inherited env); probe output `ℹ tests 4 / ℹ pass 0 / ℹ fail 4` with commit.gpgsign=true vs `ℹ pass 4 / ℹ fail 0` without; `git grep GIT_CONFIG skill/scripts/tests` -> no hits
impact_why: Anyone with signed commits or global hooks cannot run the gate; a test env leak is also a source of flakes.

title: local-forge-e2e is 32 of the suite's 39 s: run its CLI calls in-process
body:
## Summary
npm test takes 38.7 s wall; one test (local-forge-e2e) takes 32.2 s and spawns a fresh node for each of its 48 dowser CLI calls.

## Description
Measured `node --test --test-reporter=spec "skill/scripts/tests/*.test.mjs"`: 225 tests, 0 fail, duration_ms 38702. Longest: local-forge-e2e 32151 ms, mock Forge over stdio 18519 ms, sbom 14686/11077/9478 ms, snooze-until CLI 14509 ms, reflect setup 12684 ms, cli init->status 12064 ms. Files run in parallel, so wall time is the longest file. skill/scripts/tests/local-forge-e2e.test.mjs:106-107 spawns `process.execPath CLI` per call (48 `cli(` sites); a bare `dowser help` spawn costs about 180 ms here, more under the parallel load. triage-sheet.test.mjs:53 already drives the same CLI in-process through `main()`; the e2e's subject is the local Forge server, not the CLI process boundary (cli.test.mjs covers that).

## Flow
- An agent runs the gate before every handback (AGENTS.md:33)
- It waits ~39 s, ~32 s of it on one file
- Switching the e2e's cli() to in-process main() (as triage-sheet does) cuts the long pole

## Expected impact
Expected: the e2e drops to roughly the server round trips plus in-process calls; the suite wall time falls toward the next longest file (~18 s), about halving the gate.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - gate wall time
Before: 38.7 s wall; long pole local-forge-e2e 32.2 s with 48 spawned CLI calls
After: estimated ~18-20 s wall (next long pole: mock stdio 18.5 s)
Method: simulation - measured the suite and a single CLI spawn; the after figure is an estimate since the change is not made
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: spec run: `✔ local Forge, real core: push, triage over HTTP, pull, rescan, rules and outcomes round trip, idempotent (32151.0621ms)`; `ℹ duration_ms 38702.2644`; `grep -c "cli(" local-forge-e2e.test.mjs` -> 48; skill/scripts/tests/local-forge-e2e.test.mjs:107 `const r = spawnSync(process.execPath, [CLI, ...args, '--repo', repo], ...`; skill/scripts/tests/triage-sheet.test.mjs:53 `const r = await main([...args, '--repo', repo]);`
impact_why: The gate runs on every handback; halving its wall time compounds across agent sessions.

title: Unit-test triage.mjs parseDecisions: the decision grammar is reached only via the CLI
body:
## Summary
skill/scripts/lib/triage.mjs (196 lines) is the only lib module no test imports; its text parser is exercised only end to end through main().

## Description
Ground truth: of 25 modules in skill/scripts/lib, 24 are imported by a test directly or through the store.mjs facade (proposals.mjs and runs.mjs via store.mjs:23-25). triage.mjs exports triageSheet, parseDecisions and applyDecisions (lib/triage.mjs:67,91,132) and no test imports it; triage-sheet.test.mjs drives it through main() (triage-sheet.test.mjs:5,53), costing 4.3-6.7 s per case. parseDecisions turns a person's free-typed line ("1 keep, 2-3 reject not-worth-it ...") into moves - the input most likely to be malformed - so its edge cases (ranges, duplicates, unknown numbers, trailing text) are cheapest to pin as pure unit tests.

## Flow
- A person types an unusual decision line
- parseDecisions mis-splits it
- Only a slow CLI case could catch it, and only for the lines its four cases happen to type

## Expected impact
A pure test table for parseDecisions (milliseconds) covers the grammar exhaustively and leaves the CLI cases for wiring.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the decision grammar has direct coverage
Before: 0 direct imports of lib/triage.mjs; grammar covered only by CLI cases
After: a table-driven unit test of parseDecisions
Method: simulation - derived the gap from ls skill/scripts/lib vs test imports; walked range, duplicate and unknown-row lines
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: `for m in lib/*.mjs; grep -l "lib/$b.mjs" tests/*.mjs` -> `0 triage` (proposals/runs reached via lib/store.mjs `export * from './proposals.mjs'; export * from './runs.mjs';`); lib/triage.mjs:91 `export function parseDecisions(text) {`
impact_why: The one module parsing free human text has no direct, fast test.
